Between 1956 and 1963 Britain carried out nuclear tests at Maralinga in the South Australian desert, including seven atomic bombs in 1956 and 1957 and many smaller trials that scattered plutonium.

The Australian government agreed readily. The land belonged to the Maralinga Tjarutja, Aboriginal people who were moved off, and some were exposed to fallout. Servicemen too reported illness.

A royal commission in 1985 found serious failings, and Britain paid towards a clean-up. The land was returned to its owners in 2014. Compare Bikini, Moruroa and Operation Grapple.
